Good afternoon everyone and welcome back to the resumption of today's
special council meeting. As we indicated in the agenda, today is a special day
because it's an opportunity to acknowledge and recognize the Waterloo
Regional Police Service. As I think many of you know, the Waterloo Regional
Police Service was formed when the Region of Waterloo was formed back in
1973. Prior to that, there were a number of police departments including
the City of Kitchener Police Department. If I remember correctly there was even a
village of Bridgeport Police Department at the time and others. In fact
someone just recently found an old City of Kitchener police patch at a garage
sale and bought it and presented it to me at City Hall one day. But we wanted to
take this opportunity to invite Chief Crowell to Council. This week is also
Police Week in addition to it being their 50th anniversary and I believe
some of you may have had the opportunity to join in and participate on Saturday
at the open house that was hosted at WRPS headquarters on Maple Grove Road.
But really wanted to take this opportunity on behalf of Council to
thank the Waterloo Regional Police Service for the collaboration and
partnership that we've been able to have with the service over the
past 50 years. I mean you know first of what comes to mind obviously is the role
that they play together with our other emergency service partners including the
the fire department and paramedic services in terms of emergency response
in the community, obviously helping keep our residents safe and protected in terms
of some of the criminal issues that occur in the community as well as being part of
the tiered response that does occur for certain types of health issues.
But the relationship in the partnership has been much more than that over the
years, whether it's been working with downtown BIA, whether it's been working
with world councillors in response to issues in their neighborhoods,
whether it's been partnering with us on initiatives like the COPS Youth
Mentoring Program and others. I think over the past 50 years the women and
men of the Waterloo Regional Police Service have really been incredible
community partners and so we wanted to take this opportunity today to to
acknowledge them and and recognize them and so chief if I can invite you up here
and we have a plaque to present to you and it reads the council and citizens of
the city of Kitchener extend congratulations to the Waterloo Regional
Police Service on the occasion of your 50th anniversary celebrated on this day
Thank you to the women and men of the Waterloo Region Police Service who for the past 50 years have served the residents of Kitchener and our region with pride and distinction.
From the risk you take helping keep our community safe each and every day to making a difference in the lives of young people by engaging in programs like the COPS Youth Mentoring Program,
we celebrate all you have done through your passion for people and public service.
Thank you very much.
Thank you.
You only have two photographers.
Oh no, you do only have one photographer.
Wonderful.
Do you want to go back and say a few words?
Well, thank you very much for this distinguished honour.
I certainly represent many of our members currently.
About 1,200 of our members are serving the Region of Waterloo with pride and integrity
and certainly in a supportive capacity.
So in celebrating the spirit of Police Week,
which is really about building bridges
and celebrating police and community partnerships,
this is very fitting.
And as we recognize our 50 years,
I'm very proud to say that I and we are standing on the shoulders of giants,
representing six previous chiefs,
representing thousands of citizens and residents of our region
that have sought to provide enhanced public safety over many years.
We do recognize that we're in an era now where the future of public safety and the future
of policing will be all about partnerships and collaboration.
And any of the issues that we face as a community where we intersect on issues of mental health,
addictions, housing, homelessness, intimate or family partner violence, anything along
those realms, we know that we can only work together to find the best solutions forward.
So as your Chief of Police, as one community leader, this is a great honour to be recognized
today, but recognizing that our future will be with you and the citizens and all who you
represent for a more hopeful future and certainly a safer community that will be done in enhanced
partnerships as we move forward.
So on behalf of all of our members, I'm very distinguished by this honour and very grateful
for the opportunity to represent our proud members.
And we look forward to years of partnership.
Tonight we are recognizing a new auxiliary contingent, which is our reserve or volunteer
police members that serve with pride and distinction as well.
We're grateful for you hosting us in this venue tonight, and Mayor Vrbanovic and all
members of Council and all citizens of Kitchener, we're so grateful for your continued support,
trust, and your capacity to work with us in collaboration and partnership.
So thank you very much.
Thank you.
